_comment: Ops alerts as code (#201). The api applies these to the 'Overwatch Ops' Grafana org at startup (_provision_ops_alerts). Only the variable parts live here — the contact point, the root notification policy and each rule's SQL/summary. The mechanical reduce->threshold(>0) pipeline, the folder and the per-env `env` label + '[env]' summary prefix are assembled in main.py so the same file serves sandbox/staging/prod. addresses come from OPS_ALERT_EMAIL (.env). See #172/#185/#187 for how this evolved. Freshness rules (#303) use HAVING so a healthy system returns NO ROWS: the threshold is >0, and noDataState is OK, so silence means fresh. Each returns text columns alongside `value`, which Grafana turns into labels, so the e-mail says HOW stale rather than merely that something is. Adding a fourth freshness check is mechanical — copy one, change the table, the column and the interval. Freshness rules must return `value` and nothing else: returned columns are the alert's identity, and anything that moves defeats every repeat interval.

policy._comment: repeat_interval lengthened 6h->24h: a sustained-firing freshness alert (e.g. a provider block that needs a human, not a code change) should be a daily reminder, not four mails a day. Repetition is what made this the single largest source of mail in contact@. Paired with keep_firing_for on the freshness rules (main.py) so a briefly-flapping condition does not re-notify as a fresh alert.

rules.title: New user registration
rules._sql_comment: One row per new user -> Grafana turns the text columns into alert labels, so the e-mail names who signed up, their org and country (#185). value=1 keeps the reduce/threshold (>0) firing per user.
rules.sql: SELECT ru.email, ru.name, COALESCE((SELECT string_agg(o.name, ', ') FROM org_user ou JOIN organization o ON o.id = ou.org WHERE ou.sub = ru.sub), '(no org)') AS org, COALESCE(ru.country, '??') AS country, 1 AS value FROM registered_user ru WHERE ru.first_seen > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND ru.email NOT LIKE 'e2e-bot%'

rules.title: New API key requested
rules.sql: SELECT count(*) AS value FROM api_key WHERE created_at > now() - interval '15 minutes'

rules.title: Telemetry ingestion has stalled
rules._sql_comment: Returns `value` and NOTHING else. A rule's returned columns ARE its alert identity: #341 dropped the age columns but kept `newest`, which still moves when the system is SLOW rather than STOPPED — positions kept trickling, `newest` advanced, and every evaluation became a new alert. Detail belongs on the dashboard, not in the label set (#352).
rules.sql: SELECT 1 AS value FROM telemetry HAVING max(ts) IS NULL OR max(ts) < now() - interval '90 minutes'
rules.summary: No telemetry stored for over 90 minutes. The control room is up but blind — check the ingest and the SatNOGS path.

rules.title: Position propagation has stalled
rules._sql_comment: Returns `value` and NOTHING else. A rule's returned columns ARE its alert identity: #341 dropped the age columns but kept `newest`, which still moves when the system is SLOW rather than STOPPED — positions kept trickling, `newest` advanced, and every evaluation became a new alert. Detail belongs on the dashboard, not in the label set (#352).
rules.sql: SELECT 1 AS value FROM position HAVING max(ts) IS NULL OR max(ts) < now() - interval '10 minutes'
rules.summary: No positions propagated for over 10 minutes. This is local SGP4 over cached elements, so the ingest is wedged, not a provider.

rules.title: Orbital elements are stale
rules._sql_comment: Returns `value` and NOTHING else. A rule's returned columns ARE its alert identity: #341 dropped the age columns but kept `newest`, which still moves when the system is SLOW rather than STOPPED — positions kept trickling, `newest` advanced, and every evaluation became a new alert. Detail belongs on the dashboard, not in the label set (#352).
rules.sql: SELECT 1 AS value FROM elements HAVING max(epoch) IS NULL OR max(epoch) < now() - interval '24 hours'
rules.summary: Newest orbital element set is over 24h old. Positions are still being drawn, and drifting.

rules.title: A data provider refused us
rules._sql_comment: Fires on the ONSET of a refusal, not its persistence: a source that refused us in the last hour and had NOT refused us in the preceding day. CelesTrak's ask is to report the problem to a human for investigation, and investigation happens once — after that the human knows, and repeating it is how an alert becomes wallpaper (#361). Evaluated PER SOURCE so a new SatNOGS refusal is never masked by an ongoing CelesTrak one; that masking would be far worse than the noise it replaces. Sustained damage is covered separately by elements-stale. Returns `value` and nothing else, so the alert identity cannot churn (#352).
rules.sql: SELECT 1 AS value FROM (SELECT source FROM provider_refusal GROUP BY source HAVING max(ts) > now() - interval '60 minutes' AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE ts <= now() - interval '60 minutes' AND ts > now() - interval '25 hours') = 0) q HAVING count(*) > 0
rules.summary: A data provider has started refusing us — 403/429 or unreachable — and we have stopped querying it. Check provider_refusal and the ingest log. Ignoring these is what put us in CelesTrak's firewall.
